newsitem.title: BRAZIL: German coffee demand seen at 10.7 mln bags in 2000.
newsitem.headline: German coffee demand seen at 10.7 mln bags in 2000.

text.p: Coffee consumption in Germany, the largest European consumer, could reach 10.7 million 60-kg bags by the end of the century from 1O million in 1995, the head of the International Coffee Organisation (ICO) said.
Executive director Celsius Lodder's remarks were in a speech delivered by the ICO's Robert Hagen at an international coffee seminar in Rio on Tuesday.
Lodder said Germany is the world's second consumer after the United States by volume and is a highly developed market which is sensitive to price movements.
"In spite of the high overall per capita consumption of 7.4 kg per annum in 1995 there is still scope for catching up with national levels of consumption in the Eastern part of the country," he said.

This, together with a trend towards market segmentation into new products such as espresso, flavoured soluble, organic and origin gourmet, point to a continued growth rate of some 1.4 percent a year in the period 1995 to 2000, he added.
